text: Monday was the first real test after Wall Street's brutal week.
The S&P 500 rose four point seven percent. The Nasdaq rose six point five percent. And the Dow gained 1472 points.
The best day since April 2025. Strong enough to lift the S&P 500 out of correction territory, for now.
The spark: Nvidia rose 31 percent, after its board brought back Jensen Huang as CEO.
Zoom out: the S&P 500 is still about seven percent below its October record.
Next up: Dell's earnings tomorrow, and Wednesday's inflation data.
One day is not a trend. Long-term investors watch the direction, not the noise.
Your call: is the worst behind us, or still ahead? Comment BEHIND or AHEAD.
